modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.buffer_bui: Attempts to work around mods constructing BufferBuilder objects that leak memory. This can cause the JVM to crash with an hs_err_pid file in some rare cases. If you experience this type of crash, try disabling this option.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.extra_expe: Fixes the experimental feature warning being shown still being shown the first time you reopen a world that was created as experimental.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.forge_at_i: Fixes a major oversight in Forge's early error handling code that causes some parts of mods to load, but not others, which usually results in the game crashing rather than displaying the intended error screen. This issue was fixed in NeoForge, and eventually fixed in new enough versions of Forge.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.missing_bl: Hypixel sends chunks to the client that are missing some block entity data, which makes chests etc. appear invisible. This 'fixes' the problem by creating the needed data on the client. Has no effect for properly behaved servers or in singleplayer.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.restore_ol: Fixes MC-272431, which tracks the ender dragon being unable to dive to the portal as it did in 1.13 and older. This causes the dragon to fly quite a bit differently from what modern players are used to and also patches out one-cycling, so it's not enabled by default. Thanks to Jukitsu for identifying the regression in the vanilla code.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.world_scre: Fixes MC-251068, where deleting the last world takes you back to an empty world list.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.feature.blockenti: **This is a debug option and should not be enabled for regular gameplay.** Attempts to detect mods interacting with block entities on the wrong thread and crash the game with more information, rather than an unclear ConcurrentModificationException
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.feature.cause_lag: Disables the game's use of worker threads for the server and for chunk rendering. **This will make performance worse on almost all hardware**, and should only be enabled on a client, when you know exactly what you are doing, and probably only on hardware with very few (2 or less) physical CPU cores. In those rare cases, it can reduce lag spikes since there is less contention over the limited cores.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.feature.registry_: Runs the Forge loading screen on a background thread for part of the loading process, to allow progress to be shown while content is being registered. May have compatibility issues with some GPU drivers (e.g. macOS), so do not enable it by default in a modpack.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.feature.remove_ch: Prevents the Minecraft client from obtaining the keypair for chat signing. This disables the client's ability to sign chat messages (like No Chat Reports, but in a simpler, albeit less user-friendly way).
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.feature.remove_te: Prevents the Minecraft client from sending telemetry to Mojang. The telemetry is generally not relevant to them anyway for a modded instance.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.feature.suppress_: Prevents the game from logging a very long stacktrace when the narrator fails to load on Linux (usually caused by not having libflite installed).
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.chunk_meshin: Implements some minor optimizations to the vanilla chunk meshing logic (they will have no effect with a mod that replaces chunk rendering entirely).
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.compress_uni: Stores the glyphs for the Unicode font more efficiently. Kudos to @AnAwesomGuy for the trick.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_reso: LDLib compatibility patch for dynamic resources
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_struc: Improves the speed at which structures like buried treasure can be located.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.forge_regist: Fixes more oversights in Forge that lead to excessive allocation in hot registry methods.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.memoize_crea: Improves on vanilla's existing caching for creative tab contents in a way that is compatible with the timing requirements of mods like JEI/EMI. This can reduce the lag spike when opening the creative inventory for the first time in a modpack.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.potential_sp: Optimizes the Forge event for finding potential mobs that can spawn. This reduces allocations and the overhead of rebuilding a weighted list when no mods modify the potential spawns.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.ticking_chun: Optimizes chunk ticking in vanilla to reduce allocations.
modernfix.modernfix.option.mixin.perf.worldgen_all: Optimizes some world generation logic in vanilla to reduce object allocations.
modernfix.modernfix.redirector_installed: ModernFix detected that Redirector is installed. Redirector is known to cause many strange and hard-to-debug issues, and removing it is strongly recommended.

particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.AGGRE: Culls particles using their mid point. Best performance but does technically cull particles that happen to be just in-frame (but less than halfway). This is rarely noticeable, but if it is for you use Bounding Box
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.BOUND: Culls particles using the edges of their bounding box. Good performance gain and mitigates particles clipping out from the edge of the screen.
Potion particles emitted by non-player mobs will be disabled
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.NO_CU: Disables particle culling completely. Not recommended unless required.
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.OTHER: Potion particles emitted by other players (not you) will be disabled
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.async:
§6Impact: Medium§r

[true or false] When true (default), particles will tick asynchronously (not on the clients main loop). This may cause instabilities.

Particle Core will try to automatically disable this if instabilities occur. If it can't, disable this manually

When particle count is low, Particle Core will tick synchronously regardless of this setting to avoid wasting time with async overhead.
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.culli:
§cImpact: HIGH§r

How particles are culled by Particle Core. Disabling this will have a large performance impact.

§3Impact: Non-Performance§r

Particles that should be ignored by culling. This will prevent issues with particles that might behave strangely with culling, especially aggressive culling.

In particular, very large particles benefit from being blacklisted if you are using aggressive culling.
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.maxPa:
§6Impact: Medium§r

[Value between 0 and ~2 Billion] Sets how many particles can be spawned at a time. Default is 16,384.
particle_core.particle_core.particle_core_config.parti:
§6Impact: Medium§r

[Value between 0.1 and 1.0] Multiplier for how far away particles should render, based on block render distance. Default is 1 (full render distance).

Example: At 0.5, particles will only render 6 chunks away with 12 render distance.

sodium.sodium.options.animate_only_visible_text: If enabled, only the animated textures which are determined to be visible in the current image will be updated. sodium.sodium.options.attack_indicator.tooltip: Controls where the Attack Indicator is displayed on screen.
sodium.sodium.options.autosave_indicator.toolti: If enabled, an indicator will be shown when the game is saving the world to disk.
sodium.sodium.options.biome_blend.tooltip: The area (in blocks) where biome colors are smoothly blended across. Default is 5x5. Higher values will greatly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update chunks, for diminishing improvements in quality.
sodium.sodium.options.brightness.tooltip: Controls the minimum brightness in the world. When increased, darker areas of the world will appear brighter. This does not affect the brightness of already well-lit areas.
sodium.sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.name: Chunk Update Threads
sodium.sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.tool: Specifies the number of threads to use for chunk building and sorting. Using more threads can speed up chunk loading and update speed, but may negatively impact frame times. The default value is usually good enough for all situations.
sodium.sodium.options.closest_point_entity_sort: Controls how the translucent geometry of entities is sorted. "Enhanced" sorts by the closest point to the camera, which improves rendering accuracy for translucent quads with different sizes, at a small CPU cost. "Default" uses the standard sorting.
sodium.sodium.options.clouds_distance.tooltip: The distance clouds will render to. This has minimal impact on performance, and is meant for visual purposes.
sodium.sodium.options.clouds_quality.tooltip: The quality level used for rendering clouds in the sky. Even though the options are labeled "Fast" and "Fancy", the effect on performance is negligible.
sodium.sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead_limit.to: For debugging only. Specifies the maximum number of frames which can be in-flight to the GPU. Changing this value is not recommended, as very low or high values may create frame rate instability.
sodium.sodium.options.defer_chunk_updates.name: Chunk Updates
sodium.sodium.options.defer_chunk_updates.toolt: If set to "Deferred", rendering will never wait for nearby chunk updates to finish, even if they are important. This can greatly improve frame rates in some scenarios, but it may create significant visual lag where blocks take a while to appear or disappear. "Immediate" eliminates visual lag by blocking the frame until chunk updates are complete while "Soon" allows at most one frame of visual lag.
sodium.sodium.options.entity_distance.tooltip: The render distance multiplier used by entity rendering. Smaller values decrease, and larger values increase, the maximum distance at which entities will be rendered.
sodium.sodium.options.entity_shadows.tooltip: If enabled, basic shadows will be rendered beneath mobs and other entities.
sodium.sodium.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Limits the maximum number of frames per second. This can help reduce battery usage and system load when multi-tasking. If VSync is enabled, this option will be ignored unless it is lower than your display's refresh rate.
sodium.sodium.options.fullscreen_mode.name: Fullscreen Mode
sodium.sodium.options.fullscreen_mode.tooltip: Exclusive fullscreen can improve latency, but may prevent some input methods from working and slow down switching out of the game. Borderless fullscreen can cause significant performance degradation.
sodium.sodium.options.fullscreen_resolution.too:
The monitor resolution and refresh rate to be used when in fullscreen mode. Changing this option may interfere with other applications and cause a delay when switching between applications.

This is only supported on the Windows or macOS operating systems.
sodium.sodium.options.graphics_quality.tooltip: The default graphics quality controls some legacy options and is necessary for mod compatibility. If the options below are left to "Default", they will use this setting.
sodium.sodium.options.gui_scale.tooltip: Sets the maximum scale factor to be used for the user interface. If "auto" is used, then the largest scale factor will always be used.
sodium.sodium.options.hidden_fluid_culling.name: Fluid Culling
sodium.sodium.options.hidden_fluid_culling.tool: Controls how aggressively hidden fluid surfaces are culled. "Optimized" applies more aggressive culling to fluids, which can improve performance in flooded caves and underwater areas, but interruptions in the fluid surface may rarely become visible at very shallow viewing angles. "Default" keeps the standard culling behavior.
sodium.sodium.options.improved_fluid_shaping.to: Controls how fluids are shaped around waterlogged blocks. "Alternative" can improve the consistency of fluid surfaces, at the expense of not slanting the fluid in the direction of the physical flow in some situations. This does not affect the physical behavior of fluids in any way.
sodium.sodium.options.leaves_quality.name: Leaves
sodium.sodium.options.leaves_quality.tooltip: Controls whether leaves will be rendered as transparent (fancy) or opaque (fast).
sodium.sodium.options.mipmap_levels.tooltip: Controls the number of mipmaps which will be used for block model textures. Higher values provide better rendering of blocks in the distance, but could adversely affect performance with resource packs that use many animated textures.
sodium.sodium.options.particle_quality.tooltip: Controls the maximum number of particles which can be present on screen at any one time.
sodium.sodium.options.pixel_filtering_mode.name: Texel Interpolation
sodium.sodium.options.pixel_filtering_mode.tool: Controls the appearance of edges between pixels within block textures. "Nearest" mode results in sharp pixel boundaries, while "Linear" mode makes them a little blurry. "Nearest" can be slightly faster.
sodium.sodium.options.quad_splitting.name: Block Transparency Limits
sodium.sodium.options.quad_splitting.tooltip: Determines what approach is used to make translucent blocks (not entities or items) look correct even when they intersect or have unusual shapes, such as waterlogged stained glass panes. "Basic" disables this feature and such blocks may render incorrectly. "Safe" limits the amount of newly generated geometry to prevent instability in extreme cases, while "Unlimited" imposes no limit.
sodium.sodium.options.simulation_distance.toolt: The simulation distance controls how far away terrain and entities will be loaded and ticked. Shorter distances can reduce the internal server's load and may improve frame rates.
sodium.sodium.options.smooth_lighting.tooltip: Enables the smooth lighting and shading of blocks in the world. This can very slightly increase the amount of time it takes to load or update a chunk, but it doesn't affect frame rates.
sodium.sodium.options.use_block_face_culling.to: If enabled, only the faces of blocks which are facing the camera will be submitted for rendering. This can eliminate a large number of block faces very early in the rendering process, which greatly improves rendering performance. Some resource packs may have issues with this option, so try disabling it if you're seeing holes in blocks.
sodium.sodium.options.use_entity_culling.name: Use Entity Culling
sodium.sodium.options.use_entity_culling.toolti: If enabled, entities which are within the camera viewport, but not inside of a visible chunk, will be skipped during rendering. This optimization uses the visibility data which already exists for chunk rendering and does not add overhead.
sodium.sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.name: Use Fog Occlusion
sodium.sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.tooltip: If enabled, chunks which are determined to be fully hidden by fog effects will not be rendered, helping to improve performance. The improvement can be more dramatic when fog effects are heavier (such as while underwater), but it may cause undesirable visual artifacts between the sky and fog in some scenarios.
sodium.sodium.options.use_no_error_context.name: Use No Error Context
sodium.sodium.options.use_no_error_context.tool: When enabled, the OpenGL context will be created with error checking disabled. This slightly improves rendering performance, but it can make debugging sudden unexplained crashes much harder.
sodium.sodium.options.use_persistent_mapping.to:
For debugging only. If enabled, persistent memory mappings will be used for the staging buffer so that unnecessary memory copies can be avoided. Disabling this can be useful for narrowing down the cause of graphical corruption.

Requires OpenGL 4.4 or ARB_buffer_storage.
sodium.sodium.options.v_sync.tooltip: If enabled, the game's frame rate will be synchronized to the monitor's refresh rate, making for a generally smoother experience at the expense of overall input latency. This setting might reduce performance if your system is too slow.
sodium.sodium.options.view_distance.tooltip: The render distance controls how far away terrain will be rendered. Shorter distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates.
sodium.sodium.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodium.sodium.options.vignette.tooltip: If enabled, a vignette effect will be applied when the player is in darker areas, which makes the overall image darker and more dramatic.
sodium.sodium.options.weather_quality.tooltip: Controls the distance that weather effects, such as rain and snow, will be rendered.

sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.advanced_fog_setting: Unlocks per-dimension and protected gameplay fog controls. When off, the global fog settings below apply everywhere.
sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.cloud_fog.tooltip:

sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.cloud_height_overrid: Overrides dimension-defined cloud heights with Sodium Extra's Cloud Height setting.

sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.fog_shape.tooltip:

Cylindrical: Use horizontal distance with a taller vertical cap
Radial: Use true spherical distance from the camera
Planar: Use distance to the camera plane (view depth); fog shifts as you turn

sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.more_hud_overlays.to: Opens the vanilla Debug Options screen (F3+F6), which can show more debug labels on the F3 screen or as persistent overlays.
sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.panini_projection.to: Applies an experimental Panini screen projection to world rendering only. Disabled while Iris shader packs or Prevent Shaders are active.
sodium-extra.sodium-extra.option.panini_projection_st: Controls the Panini projection argument used to remap the world image after rendering.

If a selected mode prevents the game from starting cleanly, Sodium Extra will disable this option and reset fullscreen on the next launch.

structure_layout_optimizer.config.structure_layout_optimizer.dedupl: Deduplicate shuffled template pool element list

Whether to use an alternative strategy to make structure layouts generate slightly even faster than the default optimization this mod has for template pool weights. This alternative strategy works by changing the list of pieces that structures collect from the template pool to not have duplicate entries.
This will not break the structure generation, but it will make the structure layout different than if this config was off (breaking vanilla seed parity). The cost of speed may be worth it in large modpacks where many structure mods are using very high weight values in their template pools.

Pros: Get a bit more performance from high weight Template Pool Structures.
Cons: Loses parity with vanilla seeds on the layout of the structure. (Structure layout is not broken, just different)

xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_map_selection_box:
Manual - you are asked to select and confirm the world map every time you switch worlds or dimensions. 
 
 World Spawn - the world map is selected and confirmed automatically based on the world spawn point that the game client is aware of. Can break if the server is using the vanilla compass item for a custom function. 
 
 Single - each dimension has a single world map that is automatically confirmed. Useful for simple servers with a single world. 
 
 Server - install the world map mod on the server side to use this automatic mode.

xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_adjust_height_for_carpe: Subtract 1 from the height value for short carpetlike blocks, e.g. carpet, 1-layer snow, lilypad etc. This prevents such blocks from causing harsh shading on the map like a full block. Waypoints and teleportation over these blocks should make more sense too.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_arrow_color: Color of the arrow that indicates the position and the rotation of the player.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_biome_blending: Smooth out biome color edges by sampling biome colors for multiple blocks for every block on the map. Turning this off can significantly improve performance when biome color calculation is modded to be much more heavyweight than vanilla.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_allowed: Cave mode on the full screen world map. It's a mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. Cave mode is usually enabled automatically (see "Auto Cave Mode"), but can also be enabled manually on the world map screen.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_allowed_dimen: A list of dimension IDs, separated by comas, where cave mode should work on the full screen world map. If the list is empty (just []), cave mode works in every dimension.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_toggle_timer: The minimum time to wait between toggles of cave mode to prevent flickering when quickly switching between being under blocks and not. This only applies when "Auto Cave Mode" isn't redirecting to the minimap mod. The latest minimap mod has a separate setting for this as well.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_type:
The cave mode type to use when cave mode is enabled. 
 
 OFF - display above ground even when cave mode is automatically or manually enabled (same as old world map versions without cave mode) 
 Layered - separate cave maps into multiple layers depending on the used top Y 
 Full - ignore the used top Y, use a single layer for cave maps and map everything from the world top to the world bottom
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_default_cave_mode_type: The default cave mode type assigned to dimensions visited for the first time in a world/server. You can read more about cave mode types by clicking the cave mode icon on the map screen.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_detect_ambiguous_y: A single pixel on the map can contain multiple transparent layers and an opaque block under them. In older non-cache map data files, only the Y level (height) of the opaque block is stored in such cases, which often makes it unsafe to blindly teleport to the stored Y coordinate. When this setting is ON, the mod treats such map pixels as it would undiscovered chunks. It defaults to 2D waypoints and disables direct teleportation to such pixels. Disable this at your own risk!
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_display_minimap_radar: Display minimap radar on the fullscreen map. Only works when the Xaero's Minimap mod is installed.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_display_server_chunk_ra: Display a square overlay on the world map around your character corresponding to the server chunk radius (server render distance).
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_force_fast_map_writing: Bad for performance but good for mapping out servers at very high movement speeds.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_ignore_heightmaps: Some servers put custom values in the world heightmaps, which can cause incorrectly rendered maps. Sometimes it can even happen in heavily modded singleplayer worlds. This option should fix such issues at the expense of a bit of performance. Do not use unless you need to. Reenter the world after toggling the option! Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_ignore_map_file_locks: Proceed with using a map instance even if it is already being used by another process. This will cause region loading failures. Do not use this unless you know what you're doing. Relog after turning this on.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_legible_cave_maps: Use depth-based lighting in cave mode instead of actual block lighting, making it easier to mentally separate the different cave layers.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_map_teleport_command: The chat commands used on this world/server to teleport you to positions on the map. Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_max_loaded_regions: The approximate maximum number of 512x512 map regions to keep loaded, including "branch" regions rendered at lower (further) zoom levels. Other factors can increase/decrease the actual effective limit. A higher number improves performance but uses more RAM and VRAM which you can run out of.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_claims: Display chunk claims from the Open Parties and Claims mod as a colored overlay.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_claims_border_opaci: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay border color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_claims_fill_opacity: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay fill color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_player_teleport_com: The chat command used on this world/server to teleport you to other players on the map when Open Parties and Claims is installed.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_partial_y_teleportation: When teleporting to a map location, offset the Y coordinate by 0.5 to avoid falling through carpet-like blocks into the void. Otherwise, the integer Y coordinate is used.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_player_teleport_command: The chat command used on this world/server to teleport you to tracked players on the map (not regular radar). Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_skip_world_render: Skip rendering the world in the background while the world map screen is open which significantly increases the framerate. However, when this is enabled, the framerate is also manually limited to around 625 to avoid issues that come from very high framerates (such as with video recording or streaming). Some mods might not be compatible with this feature and turning it off should fix any issues but with the drawback of (usually) worse framerates.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_unlimited_zoom_in: Not actually unlimited but allows you to zoom in the fullscreen map way beyond the usual limit.
xaeroworldmap.gui.xaero_wm_box_unlimited_zoom_out:
Experimental! 
 Not actually unlimited but allows you to zoom out the fullscreen map way beyond the usual limit. It is not properly optimized for regular gameplay and should only be used when you don't care about that.
